## Employee
- Name: Sagnibha Roy (no id)
- Role: Maintenance Planner, Maintenance
- Plant / unit: Raiganj  / Unit 100

## Equipment history in the knowledge graph
- none found for this profile; interview from the profile alone and ask them to name their key equipment

topics.title: Role Overview: Daily Planning Rituals and Unwritten Workflows
topics.rationale: Captures the planner's undocumented daily routines, prioritization shortcuts, and informal coordination loops that are nowhere documented.
seed_questions: Walk me through a typical day from the moment you log in—what's the first thing you check that nobody else knows about?
What informal signals or gut feelings do you rely on when deciding which work orders to push first, beyond what the CMMS priority field says?
Are there any daily or weekly rituals you perform that a replacement would never find in a procedure?

topics.title: Key Equipment Landscape: Naming the Critical Assets and Their Undocumented Quirks
topics.rationale: No equipment is recorded in the system for this planner; they must identify the most troublesome or critical assets they plan maintenance for, revealing what the knowledge graph missed.
seed_questions: If you had to name the top five pieces of equipment that keep you up at night, what are they and why?
For each one, what is a failure mode or early-warning sign that only you seem to notice?
Are there any assets where the documented maintenance plan is completely wrong because of a 'personality' the equipment has developed?

topics.title: Maintenance Scheduling Secrets: Prioritization Beyond the CMMS
topics.rationale: CMMS schedules often fail to capture real-world constraints and political pressures that shape the planner's decisions.
seed_questions: When the schedule gets jammed, what is your mental algorithm for deciding which PM gets delayed without causing a breakdown?
Which operations or maintenance supervisors do you always talk to before finalizing the week's plan because they have information the system doesn't?
What is an example of a recurring job where the planned hours in the system are dangerously underestimated?

topics.title: Recurring Failure Patterns the CMMS Never Caught
topics.rationale: Many repeat failures are never formally trended; the planner likely knows clusters of failures that point to hidden root causes.
seed_questions: Which equipment failures keep coming back no matter what is written in the work order history?
Is there a 'bad batch' of spares or a particular installation error that keeps reoccurring but is never recorded?
What failure mode do you see creeping up that a simple condition-monitoring walkdown would catch, but nobody writes it down?

topics.title: Vendor and Contractor Intelligence: Who You Actually Call and Why
topics.rationale: Maintenance planners accumulate crucial vendor contacts and negotiation leverage that never makes it into the procurement system.
seed_questions: Which vendors or contractors have you built a relationship with that a successor absolutely must maintain, and why?
For critical equipment, who is the one person at the vendor who actually knows the fix, not just the sales pitch?
What is an unwritten rule about dealing with a specific vendor—like never ordering part X from them, or always expediting via a certain channel?

topics.title: Critical Spares Hoarding Logic: What Lives Under Your Desk
topics.rationale: Planners often squirrel away spares that are chronically short or lead time is misrepresented; these are crucial for continuity.
seed_questions: Which spare parts do you personally keep a hidden stash of because the official inventory count is never right or the lead time is a lie?
For those parts, what is the real-world lead time versus what the system says, and what is your workaround?
Is there a critical spare that isn't even listed in the BOM but you know will cause a week-long outage if it fails?

topics.title: Half-Finished Projects and Their True State
topics.rationale: Planners often inherit or oversee improvement projects that stall; the true status and blockers are rarely in official reports.
seed_questions: Which improvement or upgrade project is technically 'active' but actually dead, and what killed it?
What project were you most passionate about that never got funded, and what would it have saved?
Are there any completed projects whose documentation says they're done but the reality on the ground is a messy compromise?

topics.title: Work Instruction Gaps: What the Procedures Don't Say
topics.rationale: Standard procedures often diverge from what is actually done safely and effectively; capturing this prevents future incidents.
seed_questions: Can you think of a PM or corrective task where the written procedure would lead a new person to do something dangerous or completely ineffective?
Which job step do technicians regularly skip or modify because the documented way takes too long or requires a tool that never shows up?
Is there a lockout/tagout nuance on a specific piece of equipment that only you and a few others know?

topics.title: Communication Loops: Who Holds the Unwritten Authority
topics.rationale: Planners facilitate silent negotiations between ops, maintenance, and stores; losing these names leaves a power vacuum.
seed_questions: Who in operations always knows the real equipment condition before anyone else, and how do you get them to share it?
Which storeroom person or buyer has the magic ability to find parts that are supposedly not there, and what's their trick?
Is there a manager or engineer whose approval you always seek informally before committing to a big shutdown, even though the RACI says otherwise?

topics.title: Emergency Repair Playbook: Tribal Responses to Past Crises
topics.rationale: Crisis responses reveal deep system knowledge and unofficial coordination that no plan captures.
seed_questions: Describe the last big emergency breakdown—what did you do in the first 30 minutes that isn't written anywhere and saved the day?
Who are the external resources you call at 2 a.m. that the official call-out list doesn't include?
What is the one piece of equipment where if it fails on a weekend, you know you'll be doing a half-plant shutdown no matter what the procedure says?

topics.title: Handover: Open Risks and Successor Advice
topics.rationale: High-level transfer of risk register and critical advice to ensure continuity after departure.
seed_questions: What are the top three risks you see on the horizon that could blow up the schedule in the next six months?
If you could whisper one sentence into your replacement's ear on day one, what would it be?
Which relationship or agreement is most fragile and needs active nurture right after you leave?
